question: Does preserving scalar-input variance at initialization improve v-prediction learning and late-time sparsity at the same full-architecture short budget?
paper_basis: Continuous expression encoder is a two-layer MLP; its initialization is not specified. General Xavier initialization is a reproduction choice, not a paper requirement.

initialization.method: Rescale the original first scalar Linear weight from U[-sqrt(6/(1+768)),sqrt(6/(1+768))] to U[-1,1]; preserve zero bias and every other weight/RNG draw. This matches nn.Linear fan-in weight distribution, not its random bias initialization.
initialization.why: Fan-in scaling preserves scalar input variance independently of the expansion width; factor is derived from the distribution, not fitted to validation metrics.
initialization.interpretation_limit: Descriptive gain differences do not establish better generation; test by the preregistered same-budget objective.

initial_function: With zero output head, initial v functions and first loss match despite the changed value features. Check same indices/noise/source; do not infer learned equivalence from zero-head equality.

prelaunch_tests.result: 5 CPU cases passed1.79s: exact legacy defaults, optional projection, x/v conversion loss-gradient and Heun checks, plus single-weight rescaling, unchanged RNG and analytic value-encoder derivative scaling.

primary_objective: PDCorr+mean(PDS_L1,PDS_L2,PDS_cos), raw/nonnegative separately; same960 cells and60-condition library; all9 nonnegative metrics; paired2,000-condition bootstrap; context and variance diagnostics.
queue_dependency: Wait for x-prediction controller839902 to exit before starting; never overlap three GPU jobs.
caveat: One short seed and raw weights do not establish mature EMA superiority. This tests an unspecified implementation detail; no paper architecture, time distribution, loss, effective batch or sampling count is reduced.
